prize_parts.citation: for incorporating firm heterogeneity and selection into trade theory, and so identifying new channels for the gains from trade

statement.case_for: I moved B010 from second place in my opening ranking to my preferred prize. It combines a clearly defined conceptual advance with clean attribution and a long record of confirmation. Melitz (2003) shifted trade analysis from industries to firms and explained exporter selection, within-industry reallocation and a new gains-from-trade channel. Helpman's wider body of work, including Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple on exports versus FDI, fits a two-name citation. The framework has more than two decades of firm-level evidence behind it, and it is standard in empirical trade, in quantitative work and in policy evaluation. The reading of the openings that matters here is how robust the case is across members. Ten of eleven members place B010 in their top three, and ten of the eleven named exactly the same pair or the same pair in a different order. That is evidence about attribution stability across assessors, not a count of merit. My own B003 case (BLP and the dynamic-industry framework) is scientifically strong but has narrower support and a harder boundary question over Bresnahan, Reiss and Benkard. I therefore keep it as an alternative.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is that the prize may be seen as a refinement within a field already honoured in 2008 for new trade theory. Part of the credit also belongs to precursors outside the credited names, such as Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, and to Hopenhayn on selection. Quantitative gains-from-trade estimates depend on parametric assumptions such as Pareto productivity draws. Leaving Redding out of a three-name ballot entry also sacrifices some completeness.

responses.point: Boppart ranked B010 only sixth. He asks whether it is a distinct advance beyond Krugman's recognised work, and he ranks B019 first for its foundational collateral-constraint mechanism.
responses.response: I think B010 is distinct. The 2008 prize recognised monopolistic competition with representative firms, where gains come from variety and scale. Melitz-style selection adds a new margin, in which trade reallocates activity toward more productive firms and aggregate productivity changes. It also created a new empirical agenda built on micro data. I agree that B019 is a foundational mechanism, and I rank it as my third alternative rather than lower. But I weigh its overlap with the 2022 prize on banks and financial crises, and the competing Bernanke-Gertler-Gilchrist framing, more heavily than the B010 concern.

responses.point: Hassler ranks B010 first but flags fragmented credit, since Eaton-Kortum and Bernard-Jensen sit outside the ballot entry. He also notes that Helpman might be better matched to a broader trade framing.
responses.response: The precursor concern is real, and I take it as a qualification of the citation, not a reason to widen the prize. The core model and its theoretical architecture are credited to Melitz and Helpman, whereas the Eaton-Kortum strand is arguably a parallel contribution to quantitative trade. A narrow citation on firm heterogeneity and selection keeps it clearly separate from that strand and from Helpman's political-economy work with Grossman. I would not enlarge the laureate set to cover Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum. I would instead make sure the scientific background credits them.

responses.point: Friberg ranks B037 first. He argues that Woodford, Taylor and Gali form a coherent core despite the crowded field, and that the timing is ripe.
responses.response: I agree on the policy influence, and I ranked B037 third. My difficulty is attribution. Calvo, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Smets and Gertler have claims comparable to those of any three-name subset, and the post-2021 inflation raised open questions about the baseline model. A prize here would need a defensible boundary, which I cannot yet see. Compared with B010, where ten members converge on the same pair, B037 looks more like a synthesis of many contributions than a single laureate-able discovery.

uncertainties: Whether the Committee treats heterogeneous-firm trade as sufficiently distinct from the 2008 prize and from the Eaton-Kortum quantitative strand.
Whether Redding should be added, or Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum credited in the scientific background, since they are outside the two-name set.
Whether B003 should be preferred on its own scientific merits if B010 is judged too close to earlier trade recognition, and who the three names would be (BLP trio versus Bresnahan inclusion).
How much weight B019 should carry given the 2022 prize overlap, and whether Gertler should be credited.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile: it shows no connection to Helpman, Melitz or the other credited names on B010, B003 or B019. Disclosed for transparency only: I am an SSE affiliate alongside committee colleagues Dreber Almenberg, Friberg and Strömberg, and my own research is in matching and mechanism design, which is not the field of the preferred prize.
